Culham Trail is not bad overall. It features plenty of birds, a large river, beautiful mature trees, and is well maintained. However, it's not really my type of trail. It can get quite crowded, and parts of the route require crossing or walking alongside streets, which takes away from the natural feel. If you're looking for a peaceful, quiet hike, this may not be the best choice, as it tends to be fairly busy.

The David Culham Trail, Mississauga.  This trail is 8.2 miles return.  Anyone trying it needs to ensure they have good footwear as much of the trail has been washed away during previous floods.  However, some nice sections do exist.

We ended up having our newborn in a carrier and our toddler walked along side us. Beautiful views and the leaves have started to change. Not stroller friendly as there are big roots and parts of the bridge where a stroller would have needed to be carried. Got to see salmon in the river which our toddler loved!

Visited on a weekend. This trail is very popular  with families, runners, bikers, hikers. As the other comments mentioned, most of the trail path is indeed washed out. It’s mostly gravel path.
Credit River this time of the year (October) has many dead salmon fishes which caused bad smell as long as the trail goes beside the river.
The trail includes a few very short stretches of fall colour views. Those good spots are crowded with people taking pictures. I took a detour with the Red trail on my way back. Red trail seemed to have more fall colours than the Calhum trail.
It smells really bad of dead marine life. Lots of dead fish around the river bank.
While some parts of the trail was washed out I actually enjoyed the challenge of figuring out where to walk. I love the mix of terrain.
Did ~6 miles of this trail at a slow run and trail was a little challenging but great and easy to follow.

I recently hiked this trail and had a pretty great experience overall. One of the standout features was the lack of crowds—last week, it was pleasantly quiet, which made for a peaceful and enjoyable trek. The views along the trail were stunning and definitely worth the hike.

However, I should mention that the main road leading to the trailhead is currently under construction due to flood damage. This did cause a bit of inconvenience getting there, but it's manageable if you're prepared for a little detour or delay. Once you're on the trail, though, the natural beauty really makes up for it.

If you're looking for a serene hike with beautiful scenery, this trail is a great choice. Just be ready for some roadwork on the way in!

Culham trail has a bit of everything, from lush green enclaves to scenic views by the water and blossoming flowers. Trail is a bit slippery due to recent rain so be careful as you immerse in the many natural wonders of the trail. The best way to enjoy summer and nature.

I mostly stay around the Riverwood Conservancy and this is by far the most beautiful easy walk in Mississauga. Part of my daily exercise. Depart from the visitors parking, walk down to the river passing by the lower parking. Make my way up the ridge along the Chappell Creek and into the back trails going through the old orchard. There are several pieces of farm equipment scattered around what used to be the Zaichuk property. One used to spot deers around there. But not in the last 5 years. Last spring, on several occasions, I encountered some coyotes. I loop back to the parking and that makes for a 6 km walk. My best time is 60 minutes. I go there several times weekly. Never get tired of it. I highly recommend.

Beautiful gravel trail. Lots to see from the Credit River to beautiful untouched woods. It rained the day before and a few parts were washed out - on my way back I followed a detour from the map. I deducted a star because it leads to a residential area, then you’ll need to get back on the trail again. There were a few steep inclines (45 degree elevation at most) so it may be difficult for some to walk the trail, especially in wet conditions. 

TIPS - (1) wear boots, (2) use the map tool in this app to find alternate route, (3) give yourself a lot of extra time because there’s a lot to see! 

I’ll definitely do this trail again!

Never fails to amaze myself & the whole family. We come here almost every weekend to soak into the natural beauty around this trail without getting out of the city. The credit river that runs along the trail almost in its entirety provides a relaxing view in many spots. The thick foliage specially in the fall is so beautiful as the leaves change from green to its yellow & blazing red-orange splendour. This is probably the best spot to hike, jog & bike in the beautiful city of Mississauga.
